_comment: THE ABLATION GATE for the returns block.
Written BEFORE the block it judges, and that is the whole point. This project has
repeatedly shipped a number that turned out to measure the wrong thing, and the panel
that designed the returns block ran its own gate by hand and found the block changed
one answer of three — a closing offer that makes no claim. If that reproduces here, the
block does not ship. Declaring the criterion afterwards would let the criterion be
chosen to fit the result.
Run:  Scripts/ablate.sh --db <path> --from 2026-07-31 --to 2026-08-27
THREE ARMS, one window, same questions:
none      coverage + days only. The control.
full      coverage + days + the returns block at its real floor.
placebo   coverage + days + a returns block of the SAME ROW COUNT and the same
columns, built from subjects BELOW the floor. This arm exists because
adding 1,700 tokens of plausible text changes an answer on its own, and a
gate that only compares against the empty set measures that instead of
measuring the block.
WHAT COUNTS AS USING THE BLOCK. Mechanical, so no judge is needed and no judge can be
argued with: an answer uses the block when it names a subject key that appears in that
arm's returns table and nowhere in the coverage or days blocks. Paraphrase does not
count. If a model can answer without naming anything the block alone supplied, the
block did not contribute.
THE CRITERION, fixed here and not to be moved:
ships   full uses the block on at least 4 of the 8 questions,
AND full's usage exceeds placebo's by at least 3 questions.
cut     anything else.
The second half is the one that matters. If placebo scores as well as full, the model
is being moved by the presence of a table, not by what is in it.

window.note: Any window may be passed on the command line. This is the one the panel measured.

questions.ask: Where am I at right now, based on the last month?
questions.why: The owner's own question, verbatim in intent. The hardest one, and the one the coverage block is expected to answer by refusing.

questions.ask: Is my job affecting my personal life?
questions.why: The owner's second question. Needs contrast and coverage; the panel's dry run answered it entirely from coverage.

questions.ask: Based on what you know about me, where should I go next month?
questions.why: The owner's third. Expected to refuse outright. Included so the gate cannot be passed by counting a refusal as a use.

questions.ask: What did this month consist of?
questions.why: The plainest possible period question. If the block is ever used, it is used here.

questions.ask: What did I keep coming back to?
questions.why: Written to be maximally favourable to the block. If full does not beat placebo HERE, it does not beat it anywhere.

questions.ask: What was I doing that was not work?
questions.why: The life-versus-work question, without naming a category. No classifier may be used to answer it.

questions.ask: What is new this month that was not there before?
questions.why: Uses the first-seen column, which is the one part of the block the panel kept after deleting every last-seen field.

questions.ask: Were there stretches where I was not doing much?
questions.why: A trap. The honest answer is about coverage, not activity, and an arm that answers it from the returns table is answering wrongly.
